title: Sultanate of Agadez founded
description: The Tuareg confederation of the Aïr mountains sets up a sultanate at Agadez, the caravan city between Timbuktu and the Mediterranean.

title: Sultanate of Damagaram founded
description: Kanuri aristocrats make Zinder the walled capital of Damagaram, the strongest state between Kano and Bornu through the next century.

title: Heinrich Barth in Zinder
description: The German scholar crossing from Tripoli to Lake Chad stays with the sultan, one of the first Europeans to report on the region.

title: Voulet–Chanoine mission ends in mutiny
description: After a march of massacres across the Niger hinterland, the two French officers are shot by their own Senegalese soldiers, a scandal Paris long hushes up.

title: French occupy Zinder
description: Lieutenant Pallier of the Voulet–Chanoine mission storms Damagaram's capital after brief resistance, breaking the strongest sultanate in the region.

title: French take Agadez
description: French columns enter the Tuareg capital, whose sultan remains on his throne as their figurehead.

title: Niger Military Territory at Zinder
description: France separates its lands east of the river as a military territory ruled from Fort Cazemajou.

title: Kaocen rebellion
description: Kaocen Ag Mohammed, with Sanusi support from Libya, besieges Agadez through the winter; its relief and the rebellion's crushing end Tuareg independence in the Aïr.

title: Capital moves to Niamey
description: The administration shifts from Zinder to a riverside village that grows into the capital.

title: Independence from France
description: Niger becomes independent with Hamani Diori as president.

title: Uranium mining begins at Arlit
description: The first uranium is shipped from the desert workings at Arlit, soon the country's chief export.

title: Kountché seizes power
description: With the Sahel drought starving the country, Lieutenant-Colonel Seyni Kountché overthrows Diori and rules for thirteen years.

title: Ali Saibou succeeds
description: Kountché dies of cancer and his army chief takes over, nudging Niger toward civilian rule.

title: First Tuareg rebellion
description: A reprisal massacre at Tchin Tabaraden sets off five years of Tuareg insurgency in the north, ended by a peace accord.

title: Baré Maïnassara coup
description: The army chief overthrows the elected government, then wins a presidential vote widely seen as rigged.

title: Baré assassinated
description: Presidential guards shoot Baré at the airport; the junta that follows hands power to elected civilians within the year.

title: Second Tuareg rebellion
description: The Niger Movement for Justice demands a share of the uranium wealth and lays mines around Agadez until Libya brokers peace.

title: Tandja's third-term crisis
description: President Tandja dissolves the courts and parliament and forces through a referendum extending his rule, isolating Niger abroad.

title: Coup ousts Tandja
description: Soldiers storm the palace during a cabinet meeting and end the presidency of Mamadou Tandja, promising elections.

title: Issoufou takes office
description: Mahamadou Issoufou becomes president after elections the junta kept its word on, a rare clean handover.
